lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: sequences as functions on the integers
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: sequences as functions on the integers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time crosses the horizontal axis. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the average rate of change over the flight
the maximum, giving the greatest height
a zero, giving the time the projectile returns to ground level
the y-intercept, giving the launch height

items.prompt: Does the relation x = y², for real y define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
choices: Yes; each input appears once, so each has exactly one output.
Yes; repeated outputs are allowed, only repeated inputs with different outputs are not.
No; the input 4 gives both y = 2 and y = −2.
No; the input 1 is paired with both 3 and 8.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A machine starts with 60 components and consumes 5 per hour. It can run for at most 34 hours. What is the domain of C(h) = 60 − 5h in this context?
A sequence is defined by a(1) = 10 and a(n) = a(n − 1) + 5 for n > 1. Find a(29).
In a modelling context, the graph of a projectile’s height against time reaches its highest point. Which feature is this, and what does it mean?
choices: the y-intercept, giving the launch height
the x-intercept, giving the landing time
the maximum, giving the greatest height and the time it occurs

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Does the set {(1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (5, 4)} define y as a function of x? Justify the decision.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
